question: For each of the 40 states and D.C. whose individual income tax the 56-place research marks YES, and for Montana, whose 2026 status it marks UNKNOWN: (1) the 2026 employer withholding method or table for a resident employee with the state's default exemption or allowance certificate, for weekly and daily pay; (2) whether wages are taxed where the employee lives, where the work is done, or both, and any reciprocity agreements; (3) the annual return due date and the state's rule for an unpaid balance (penalty, interest, notices). Start with the flat-rate states (Arizona, Colorado, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Utah), which need the least. Mark each figure with its source and tax year; say UNKNOWN where nothing is verified.
requestedBy: filed by the Taxes people and businesses pay thread, building on who-pays-which-taxes-56-places

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Gives rates and coverage as YES/NO/UNKNOWN; marks withholding method, cadence and payment timing UNKNOWN.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: The paycheck assessment records this tax as UNKNOWN with no amount, because the 56-place research does not carry what is asked here.

title: How much state income tax is withheld from a paycheck, in each state that has one
usableAnswer: One row per place: withholding formula or table for weekly and daily pay, residence versus work-place rule, reciprocity partners, due date, and unpaid-balance penalty and interest, each cited.
whyItMatters: A paycheck in any of these places records the state income tax as UNKNOWN today. The nine no-tax states already record a lawful $0 with the state's own statement behind it; this is what the other 41 places need to do the same with a real amount.
